title: Black queer men in Birmingham | BLKOUT in Birmingham
metaDescription: For Black queer men in and around Birmingham — Handsworth, Lozells, Digbeth, Balsall Heath: what's here, what's beside us, what's worth the journey, and a community-owned door into BLKOUT.

landmark.alt: Pencil sketch of the Bullring Bull statue outside Birmingham's Bullring shopping centre, with the BLKOUT roundel set into a full moon above

hero.kicker: One community. Many doors. This is BLKOUT's first outside London.
hero.heading: BLKOUT in Birmingham
hero.standfirst: BLKOUT is a community-owned co-operative for Black queer men across the UK. In London the community came first and the door followed; here it's the other way round — and Handsworth already has the numbers.
hero.standfirstMore: Handsworth and Lozells hold the second-largest Black population of any city in the country. What's missing isn't the men — it's the surface where we become visible to each other. This door starts that: real nights running, real history already here, told properly below.

quiz.heading: Know your Birmingham?
quiz.sub: Three questions. No prizes except the stories.

questions.q: Birmingham's oldest surviving gay venue, the Nightingale Club, started life in 1967 as what?

options.t: A rundown Indian restaurant on Camp Hill

questions.reveal: Laurie Williams and Derek Pemberton paid £600 for it — and ran it as a member-owned club from the start, not just a business, so every member had a say in what happened to it.

questions.q: Yshee Black, on why she mentored Black Peppa into drag in Birmingham: "We don't have that many Black queer acts on the Birmingham scene, so to see someone as..." what?

options.t: "new to the scene and hungry to learn"

questions.reveal: "...I just knew I had to give them any knowledge and wisdom I had." Black Peppa went on to win EuroDrag England (2020) and compete on RuPaul's Drag Race UK.

questions.q: UNMUTED, Birmingham's QTIPOC community group, was founded by someone who also co-leads which national organisation?
questions.reveal: Suriya Roberts-Grey founded UNMUTED and co-leads Colours Youth Network, which supports LGBTQ+ young people of colour (16-25) UK-wide.

scores.three: You know Birmingham's own record. Now help us find what we're still missing.
scores.two: Close — and honestly, there's more we haven't found yet than we have.
scores.low: Fair enough — this is BLKOUT's first door outside London, and the history below is thinner than we'd like. Help us fill it in.

here.heading: Here in Birmingham
here.intro: What's organised in the city for Black queer men and Black LGBTQ+ people, as we find it — and help us find more.

entries.name: Fruit Punch
entries.note: Black & POC Queer-led collective — monthly Black and POC LGBTQIA+ Social at The Night Owl, 17-18 Lower Trinity Street, Deritend.

here.quietNote: Checked 23 September 2026 (open-source only, not yet confirmed by a direct message to the organisers) — Fruit Punch looks current and real. DLPlug's Stripped Birmingham is not listed here: checked directly against dlplug.com's own Birmingham page, which shows 'no events at the moment' and still names Just For You Sauna, 40 Summer Hill Rd — a venue that has since closed (the same team opened Yumbo, Hockley Hill, 14 Aug 2026, in its place). DLPlug itself is very much live nationally (Shoreditch, elsewhere); its Birmingham chapter is quiet right now, not gone — worth a direct check before ruling it out for good.
here.recentlyNote: No BLKOUT-run event has ever happened in Birmingham, as far as this recon found (checked the events table, the story archive, and the internal archive DB — all clean). Unlike Camden or Croydon, there's no 'recently' strip to draw on yet — that's the honest state, not a gap in the search.

besideUs.heading: Beside us in the city
besideUs.intro: Neighbours doing good work in Birmingham. Use them — and tell them we sent you.

entries.name: UNMUTED
entries.note: A voluntary group providing safe space for QTIPOC in Birmingham since at least 2018 — monthly meetups at Impact Hub Birmingham, a QTIPOC book club at Waterstones, a POC contingent at Birmingham Pride, group travel to UK Black Pride. Founded by Suriya Roberts-Grey.

entries.name: Colours Youth Network
entries.note: UK-wide network supporting LGBTQ+ young people of colour (16-25) — co-led by UNMUTED's founder, Suriya Roberts-Grey.

entries.name: Birmingham LGBT
entries.note: The city's main LGBTQ+ centre — runs sexual health clinics, a community directory (via BVSC), and general support services.

entries.name: CineQ / SHOUT Festival
entries.note: SHOUT is Birmingham's queer arts festival (~15 years running); CineQ, founded by Rico Johnson-Sinclair, is its QTIPOC-focused film strand — its 'Black Magic' shorts programme is specifically about Black queer experience.

worthTheJourney.heading: Worth the journey
worthTheJourney.intro: Black queer men have never let a city boundary decide where community happens. Where you're centred, not just welcome:

entries.name: Black Beetle Health
entries.note: The UK's only public health charity focused specifically on health inequalities for LGBTQ+ Black people and people of colour — resources, research and signposting, reachable from anywhere.

services.heading: Look after yourself
services.intro: Free, confidential, no GP needed, no judgement — and your business stays yours.

entries.name: Birmingham LGBT Centre Sexual Health Services
entries.note: LGBT sexual health clinics Wed/Thu 9am-5pm — rapid HIV testing, assisted testing, free STI kits.

entries.name: Umbrella Health Birmingham
entries.note: NHS sexual health services, run in partnership with Birmingham LGBT Centre.

entries.name: Find your nearest NHS clinic
entries.note: Every NHS sexual health service near you — testing, treatment, PrEP — searchable by postcode.

numbers.heading: The numbers nobody counts
numbers.body: Critical Frequency's own national dossier — the same demographic analysis behind every other door's figure — puts the West Midlands (Birmingham) estimate at 2,000-3,000 Black queer men, drawn from a UK-wide working estimate of 50,000-65,000, built from Census data, asylum statistics and age demographics. It's a regional figure, not a Birmingham-city-only one — Handsworth and Lozells hold the second-largest Black population of any UK city, but the estimate itself is counted at West Midlands scale.
numbers.history:
## 1948 — a company passing through

In 1948, Berto Pasuka's Les Ballets Nègres — Europe's first Black-led dance company, and the anchor of BLKOUT's own Westminster door — played Birmingham to reviews calling it 'vital and compelling'. A touring company passing through, not a resident — colour here, not the anchor.

## 1968–1979 — Stuart Hall

From 1968 to 1979, Professor Stuart Hall — Jamaican-British, one of the most consequential Black British intellectuals of the century — directed the University of Birmingham's Centre for Contemporary Cultural Studies, the founding institution of British Cultural Studies. Not a queer figure in this history, but a foundational one for how Black Britain has thought about representation ever since.

## 1968–1992 — Handsworth's magazine

Hall's own thread leads to this door's strongest anchor. From 1978, a room above a Grove Lane terrace in Handsworth held Ten.8, a quarterly photography magazine. In 1987, Ten.8 published Rotimi Fani-Kayode's homoerotic portraits after a London magazine rejected them as 'too controversial' — and Fani-Kayode went on to co-found Autograph, which still champions Black photographers today. Ten.8's own final issue (1992) was co-edited by Stuart Hall. A Handsworth magazine gave a young Black queer photographer the platform London wouldn't.

## 2016–2018 — BLKOUT's own record

BLKOUT's own record starts in October 2016: Raurie 'Rawzilla' Williams — the 'First Gay Grime MC', viral in 2013 — was one of our writers, Birmingham-based. He wrote about Birmingham's Hurst Street: 'Where are my dark skin brothers?' Two years later, BLKOUT backed a different Birmingham member: Aaron Lambert's debut one-man show, Candid, at Canada Water Theatre, 9 November 2018. Rob designed the promotional images; asked where he was 'really' from, Aaron answered: 'Lol. My grandparents were born in Jamaica.' It played to a full house.

## Today

By 2018, Suriya Roberts-Grey had founded UNMUTED, a QTIPOC group meeting monthly at Impact Hub Birmingham. A Black queer drag lineage took root too: Yshee Black mentored newcomer Black Peppa, who went on to win EuroDrag England (2020) and compete on RuPaul's Drag Race UK. Today, Fruit Punch runs a monthly Black and POC social at The Night Owl, Deritend — real nights, running now.

## What's still missing

One thing this door is still looking for: a figure who lived and organised here across a life, the way Ivor Cummings anchors Croydon. Ten.8's Handsworth moment is real, but Fani-Kayode lived and worked in London. The search continues — literally: Dr Nathaniel Adam Tobias Coleman, born in Birmingham, is writing a fresh history of Section 28 and the Black Queer activists who resisted it. His work sits exactly where this door does.

» None of this happens without the people already building it — see who's here in Birmingham right now.

entries.title: I won't settle for Gary and his cats

faq.a: No — BLKOUT is registered in Croydon, with doors in boroughs across London. This would be our first door outside London, and it's still a draft.

faq.q: Where can I meet other Black queer men in Birmingham?
faq.a: Fruit Punch runs a monthly Black and POC social at The Night Owl, Deritend, checked 23 Sep 2026. Not yet confirmed by a direct message to the organisers.

door.heading: Be met
door.tender: Come as you are. We answer.
door.intro: Leave your name and we'll keep you posted about Birmingham — what's on, what's starting, and how to be part of it. This goes to BLKOUT, a co-operative owned by its members. No engagement machinery, nothing sold onward — just a community that answers.

truer.heading: Make it truer
truer.intro: This is our thinnest door's history yet, and it needs Birmingham's own record more than most. If you know UNMUTED, Fruit Punch, DLPlug's Birmingham nights, or a piece of this city's Black queer history we haven't found — tell us.

footer.line: BLKOUT is a member-owned Community Benefit Society for Black queer men in the UK. One platform, many doors — this would be the first outside London.
